title: Accessibility: WCAG and levels A, AA and AAA

videos.script: Here is a booking page. It works. You pick a show, type your name, press Book, and the seat is yours. {{page}} Now put the mouse away. Press Tab. The focus jumps to the name field first, then up to the links, and the Book button never comes. {{keyboard}} Turn the screen off and listen instead. The logo has no words. The name field has no question. {{reader}} None of that fails a functional test. So how do you say it is wrong, in a way nobody can argue with? {{question}} With WCAG. Four principles, thirteen guidelines, and eighty-six success criteria, each one a sentence a page meets or does not. {{layers}} Each criterion has a level. A is the floor. AA is what the law and the contracts ask for. AAA is for where it fits. {{levels}} In this lesson you write the page with eight defects in it, on purpose. {{defects}} And you compute one number that nobody should judge by eye: the contrast between a grey and a white. {{contrast}} The next three lessons find the defects, and fix them.
